questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study destination was chosen based on a place that is different from my home city. The country and especially the city is a very beautiful place and is very well suited for an Erasmus exchange. Besides, Charles University which is a very superior university, gave rise to a lot of nice courses. Also courses that I won't be able to take at home. These are the reasons for my choice of study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine, however it was sometimes difficult to get in touch with the Erasmus office it you were in doubt of specific things, which were difficult to find information on the website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Everyone was very nice, and especially the orientation day was a good way to start the semester. Both to meet the other students but also to meet other Czech students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was much easier when you had arrived and it was possible to talk to them personally, where they were very helpful and you could get all the help you needed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through AirBnB and therefore it was very easy to find something. Also to find something in a location you would like to stay at which was very nice as well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you come by yourself, I would recommend to find a shared flat, so you have flatmates to live with. I was so lucky to come with my boyfriend and therefore it was nice to have an apartment with him, but if I were to travel alone, I would have liked to stay with others. A shared flat would have been nice for that purpose.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy however, it took a long time, as everyone needed to be there in person and get the signature in hand. It was not possible to register online, which could have been easier and faster. However, it was straight forward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At the orientation day you heard all the important information needed and then everyone could one at a time go to the person in charge and get registered with a signature.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always contact them through email and then meet them at the Erasmus office close to campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took a long time to figure out which courses I could get, as it was not easy to find out which days at which times they were at. When I had figured that out, I could register for the courses after changing my Learning Agreement which I then had to get signed by three different people. Then it was different for each course how to register and if they were in one or the other website.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know that it will take time, as it is a new system you need to learn and a lot of documents need to be signed by different people, so have patient. You will succeed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Each course was very different. I had one practical laboratory course, which was very beginners friendly and I had already done all the things we learned there. Another course which was Cytometry was difficult as it is a difficult method but it was very nice to have. The other courses were at a good level and compatible to mine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different as most courses were only 3 credits where I am used to at least 7,5 credits per course. I had approximately one lecture per week and then some I had also practicals once a week. The lectures were 1,5 hours long and there were no breaks, whereas at UCPH we usually have a short break each 30-45 minutes. For all the courses I didn't read any books as it was optional. Slides from the lectures was used to study for the exam, which was very new for me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Parasitology, Botany of Non-vascular Plants, Proteins of Signaling Cascades, Cytometry, Molecules of Life and Mutations, Practical Molecular Biology, Model Organisms in Developmental Biology, Czech Language course for beginners.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Proteins of Signaling Cascades, Cytometry and Molecules of Life and Mutations, as they are good to have and understand. However, Cytometry is very difficult so you should know that before choosing it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any unexpected costs. Prague was very nice and a cheap place to live.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: With my student ID I could get a lot of nice discounts which were unexpected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I danced ballet at an international ballet school in Prague twice a week which was very nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had multiple groups of students planning trips and events for Erasmus students which was nice in the beginning to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participate in as many events in the beginning as possible as it was nice to meet people who also were looking to meet new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit all the nice places in middle of Prague, like Old Town, Charles Bridge, Prague Castle and so on. Then it is very easy to go to day trips to a lot of nice cities like Kutna Hora, Cesky Krumlov and Pilsen. It is also easy to go hiking in Czech Republic where you can see the beautiful nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, and then when I had learned a little bit of Czech it was nice to use in super markets and shops. A lot of old people don't speak english, but a lot of young people do.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't hang out with a lot of local students as I had a lot of courses with other Erasmus students. I talked a lot with the local students who organized the trips and were a part of Erasmus Club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the local people weren't that polite as I am used to back home. However, you would quickly get used to it, and then when someone is very polite you get very happy about that person.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the nature in Czech Republic, and a quick train ride led to a beautiful little hiking trip. Prague is a very hilly city and gave rise to a lot of nice views of the city. The city is so beautiful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. There are a lot of campuses around the city and also outside of Prague. 2. Don't expect the lecturers to be very structured. 3. Their english can vary. However, most of the teachers are very nice even though some of them can seem a little scary. Since it is a little more relaxed and the courses are so small you also get the chance to talk more with the teachers.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the small classes as you will get close to your colleagues and maybe even the teachers.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was amazing to live in such a beautiful city that Prague is and enjoy it with all the other Erasmus students that were all open and adventurous like myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It could be challenging with the lack of english the older people had. For example when I had to go to the foreign police and register myself in the country, they couldn't speak one word of english and it was difficult to tell them what we needed to do. Also, when I had a course outside of the city center, I had to be allowed to enter the campus and they couldn't speak english either. So sometimes they wouldn't even let me in even though I was a student. I learned in the end how to manage it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
I really loved to live in Prague and can't wait to visit the city again in the future. I have met wonderful people that I will cherish for life. 
Now I can't wait to get back and have the routine of UCPH that I will cherish much more now. the structure and the teachers and so on.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
